claim: Software engineering must preserve system intent
counterexample: A software roadmap that tracks story points but not system constraints can be on schedule and still unsafe or unusable.

claim: Traceability connects implementation to justified choices
counterexample: Code commit hashes without semantic links to requirements are provenance, not complete traceability.
Relying on “the system model says so” is especially dangerous when model authors and software teams use different meanings of availability or real time.

claim: Architecture is the set of costly-to-reverse decisions
counterexample: Microservices do not automatically confer scalability or reliability; each network boundary is another partial-failure mechanism.

claim: Iteration must still produce system evidence
counterexample: Velocity measures delivery throughput, not mission effectiveness or safety confidence.

claim: Quality attributes must be formulated as scenarios
counterexample: Architecture review scores without measured scenarios produce false precision.

claim: Distributed systems convert partial failure into design work
counterexample: Global locks are rarely a free substitute for carefully scoped invariants and operational recovery plans.

claim: Performance and security share resource budgets
counterexample: A performance test conducted with authentication disabled cannot support claims about the deployed secured system.

claim: Dependability is a claim supported by argument and evidence
counterexample: Adding probabilities to unvalidated common-cause events can create a misleadingly precise safety number.

claim: The verification chain includes build identity
counterexample: A thousand passing tests can leave a critical hazard uncovered if coverage is counted without requirement and scenario semantics.

claim: Operations is part of the design
counterexample: Operational dashboards that show only CPU and HTTP success can miss mission harm; include user-impact and safety-relevant metrics.

claim: The final baseline is a reasoned technical argument
counterexample: Technology trend assessments should include opportunity cost, migration risk and the evidence that would cause a recommendation to change.
